text:
redwood-incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P1 — lighthouse-med (private gateway) egress failures detected at 13:02 UTC. Symptoms: ~40% of requests to vendor api.healthinsight.com timing out, elevated 5xx from dedicated pool us-east-1-dp-3; NLB target group 10.0.2.x reported Unhealthy. Paging oncall network. Runbook: https://go.redwood/runbooks/vpc-egress-ppi

oncall-alex: i'm on it — starting tcpdump/target checks. tagging @sre-maya for NLB/sg path.

lighthouse-oncall: confirmed from our side — all traffic from our private-gw in us-east-1 failing; other customers unaffected. this started ~13:01 UTC. we pushed a canary earlier but reverted before 12:50.

sre-maya: rolling through checks: NLB (nlb-prod-gw-us-east) shows some targets flapping in TG: tg-0a1b2c3d, healthcheck reports connection reset. security groups for instances look unchanged. route table for private-gw still points to nat-attach-01. capturing tcpdump now.

eng-jordan: past incidents reminder — sometimes the ALB->NLB path gets stuck if SG states exceed conntrack on kernel after long-lived flows. can we check conntrack counts on gateway instances?

platform-diego: seeing elevated conntrack on gw-attach-01: conntrack_count=198723 (limit 200000) — trending up. that could explain new TCP resets to targets.

oncall-alex: ok high conntrack. immediate mitigation options: 1) increase conntrack limit on gateway(s) (short-term), 2) rotate gateway ENI to force conntrack state flush (fast), 3) shift lighthouse-med to dedicated ephemeral egress pool for customer isolation (medium). leaning to 2 + 3.

sre-maya: agree. doing ENI rotation on gw-attach-01 now (will trigger brief flow disruption for that instance only). I'll run:```bash
# detach secondary ENI to force traffic onto alternate gw
aws ec2 detach-network-interface --attachment-id eni-attach-0abc1234
sleep 10
# reattach
aws ec2 attach-network-interface --network-interface-id eni-0abc1234 --instance-id i-0f123456 --device-index 1
```

lighthouse-oncall: :white_check_mark: we can tolerate a ~30s blip. moving to dedicated pool would be ideal long-term, let us know ETA.

platform-diego: meanwhile i'll bump conntrack to buy time:```bash
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=300000
# persist in /etc/sysctl.d/99-conntrack.conf
``` applying on gw-attach-01 and gw-attach-02 now.

oncall-alex: doing targeted NLB target deregister/reg to drain bad targets to healthy ones while rotation happens:```bash
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:tg/tg-0a1b2c3d --targets Id=i-0f123456
sleep 15
aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:tg/tg-0a1b2c3d --targets Id=i-0f123456
```

sre-maya: tcpdump shows many CLOSE_WAIT and TIME_WAIT on connections from gw to vendor IPs; SGs are not explicitly blocking, looks like upstream vendor is dropping half the TCP sess. i'm opening a support ticket with vendor but we should isolate customer traffic.

eng-jordan: propose reroute for lighthouse-med to dedicated egress pool (dedicated-pool-7) in us-east-1, which has spare capacity. Steps: update route table for the customer's private subnet to point at the transit attachment for dedicated pool. Minimal DNS change required. Estimated switch time 5-7m with rollback option.

lighthouse-oncall: please proceed. we need minimal customer downtime — prefer warm handoff window. can you post exact commands so our network team can approve quickly?

oncall-alex: executing switch now. commands (internal tooling):```yaml
# route-update (internal cli)
redwood route update --tenant lighthouse-med --from private-gw-us-east --to dedicated-pool-7 --mode live --drain 120
``` applying in 30s.

redwood-incident-bot: Action started by oncall-alex: route-update job 34567 queued. Notifying dedicated pool owners.

platform-diego: conntrack bump applied on both gw nodes. ENI rotation completed on gw-attach-01; target flapping reduced. monitoring metrics.

ops-night-oncall: taking night handoff in 10m. current status?

oncall-alex: route-update job 34567 completed at 13:07:12 UTC. lighthouse-med traffic now flowing via dedicated-pool-7. healthchecks for vendor endpoints improved from 65%->95% success. early logs show error rate back to baseline.

lighthouse-oncall: can confirm our API calls to api.healthinsight.com are normal again. thank you — we saw ~3m of elevated errors.

sre-maya: leaving next steps in runbook: 1) follow up with vendor for their reported drops, 2) investigate conntrack tuning and add autoscaling alert if >75% of limit, 3) schedule migration of lighthouse-med to permanent dedicated pool to avoid shared-gw saturation. tagging @eng-jordan for long-term.

eng-jordan: will open an RFC for permanent dedicated pool and autoscale policy. estimate 2 weeks for config + testing.

redwood-incident-bot: INCIDENT P1 mitigated -> reduced to P2 at 13:12 UTC. handoff to ops-night-oncall. summary: conntrack exhaustion on customer private gateway caused NLB target resets; mitigations: conntrack bump + ENI rotation + live route shift to dedicated-pool-7. Customer impact: lighthouse-med ~3-4 minutes elevated errors. Runbook link: https://go.redwood/runbooks/vpc-egress-ppi

ops-night-oncall: ack, taking ownership. will monitor for 2 hours and confirm when clearing. good notes. :thumbsup:

lighthouse-oncall: thanks all. we'll follow up if we see anything else from the vendor side.

oncall-alex: closing active paging for network now, handing to night. logs retained under incident-34567.

ops-night-oncall: closing thread when verified healthy for full 2h window.
